take_homes: split agents only when they need different access, dialect or stance. otherwise one good prompt is enough.
give the synthesizer a framework like Rumelt's kernel so it picks one answer and doesn't average the views.
handoffs between agents lose things quietly, like one of two numbers, and nobody checks whether the final briefing is true.

monday.move: look at the handoff between the two agents in our sales-ops pipeline for dropped numbers or flattened wording, and put in a propose-then-approve step for anything that posts outward
monday.stop_condition: we find no lost or changed facts in 10 sampled handoffs
monday.blocker: finding time, and I still don't have a clean way to check whether the output is true

misconception.why: the two-numbers example, then 'nothing here checks any of it', made me see that an agent can be good and the output still wrong at the handoff. I still think the review step is slow, but I wouldn't call it for beginners now.

one_line: solid on when not to split and why a framework stops the mush. the first half is slow for anyone who already runs agents, but the seams bit was new and a bit uncomfortable.
